ops.title: The 2026-07 go-nfsv4 30%-CPU spike was the June carve-outs lost in the holderfs cutover; fixed in cc-pool v0.36.3 (Manifest emits EntrySymlink for all shared base entries) — key invariants, measurement, and what remains
ops.body:
The 2026-07-03 "go-nfsv4 at ~30% CPU" report was a REGRESSION of the June perf pass
([[claude-pool-fuse-perf-pass]]): the Phase 3B holderfs cutover (711acec0) collapsed the
carve-out set to `SharedEntries={"plans"}`, so all bulk claude I/O (projects/, statsig,
session-env, shell-snapshots, history.jsonl, …) rode through fuse-t NFS again. Measured
before: ~1,090 GETATTR/s + 420 LOOKUP/s + 58 OPEN/s; go-nfsv4 CPU = GC churn from op volume.
After the fix: 81 GETATTR/s / 31 LOOKUP/s / 2 OPEN/s, go-nfsv4 ≈0% CPU.

**Fix (cc-pool v0.36.3, commit ba52f514)**: `PoolContentSource.Manifest` snapshots base's
top level per mount Build and emits every shared entry as `content.EntrySymlink`
(zero-syscall `sharedEntry` serving in holderfs — mechanism was already there, exercised by
plans). One predicate `sharedTopLevel` in `internal/overlay/classify.go`; `Classify` agrees
for tree-mode consumers. `SkipPrefixes` gained `.fuse_hidden`/`.nfs.` (silly-rename litter).

**Cardinal invariant learned (adversarial review caught a real credential leak)**: the
manifest-symlink set must be provably DISJOINT from the holder's private-redirect set.
`PrivateEntry` is dot-anchored but holder `PrivatePrefixes` matches bare `HasPrefix` — a
`.credentials.json~` sibling would have been BOTH private-redirected and symlinked into
shared base (symlink wins in holderfs → pool account reads plain claude's tokens).
`carveOutPrivate` (case-folded bare-prefix over the same `PrivatePrefixes` slice +
`ExcludedEntries`) closes it; mutation-verified negative tests pin it. Any future carve-out
logic must reject by bare prefix over `PrivatePrefixes`, not by `PrivateEntry` alone.

**Manifest propagation fact**: holderfs fetches the manifest over the bridge ONCE per mount
Build (`holderfs.go:122`) — a manifest change needs a daemon restart (bridge side) + a
remount per account. Symlink→fuse `--force` works under live sessions; fuse→fuse needs a
graceful-unmount bounce (fails clean EBUSY while sessions hold fds).

**Rollout state 2026-07-03**: 9/10 accounts re-fused on the new manifest; ~291 stale
`.fuse_hidden`/`.nfs.` litter files deleted from ~/.claude. acct-06 left pending: row was
symlink with the OLD fuse mount stale-pinned by 3 pre-existing sessions + private files
stranded in acct-06.private by an interrupted migration — needs those sessions relaunched,
then the orphan sweep unmounts and `ccp migrate --to fuse --account 6` completes.

**Phase B RESOLVED — cc-pool opt-in ABANDONED on VM evidence (2026-07-03).** fusekit v0.26.0
ships the generic capability: `MountOptions.AttrCache` honored on darwin (default false =
`noattrcache`; opt-in leaves go-nfsv4's default-on cache) + `AttrCacheTimeout`
(`-o attrcache-timeout=<secs>`, a real fuse-t option proven from its dylib option table),
plumbed additively through MountSpec/mountd.Request/HolderSpec, plus the
`validate-attrcache.sh` VM gate (vmstress `tornread`: every through-mount synth read must
parse as a complete envelope, Gen monotonic, `--writer` measures staleness). **The gate
failed 2/2 within seconds of churn**: synth documents whose size changes and are promptly
re-read (cc-pool's `.claude.json` exact shape) tear in BOTH directions under any nonzero
TTL — stale-small clamps a grown doc mid-JSON; stale-large over-reads a shrunk doc into
NUL padding ('\x00' after top-level value). Attr stabilization can't help (size legitimately
changes; go-nfsv4 has no fs-driven invalidation). **cc-pool must NEVER set AttrCache=true**
— the contraindication is in the field's godoc; the scenario is the regression gate. No
holder swap was needed (default-off = no behavior change). Post-carve-out CPU was already
~0%, so nothing was lost. Related: [[fusekit-content-over-rpc]], [[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]].
